journals.name: Washington Law Review
journals.basis: reported by the journal's editors in a Scholastica interview (Aug 2020): moved to blind article selection in summer 2018

journals.name: U.C. Irvine Law Review
journals.basis: bracketed by archived pages: absent Apr 2019, present Oct 2019

journals.name: Michigan Law Review
journals.basis: announced: policy starts February 2020; Dec 2019 archived page has no blind-review text

journals.name: Cornell Law Review
journals.basis: announced: double-blind pilot starting Fall 2020 (Vol. 106); Oct 2020 archived page refers to 'our new blind review policy'

journals.name: Maryland Law Review
journals.basis: announced: starts February 4, 2020 (Vol. 80)

journals.name: UC Law Journal
journals.basis: bracketed by archived pages: absent Dec 2019 (Vol. 71 page: CV with every submission, no anonymous route), present Feb 2020 (Vol. 72)

journals.name: Yale Law Journal
journals.basis: bracketed by archived pages: the journal's online submission form of 30 Oct 2004 lists upload steps and invites a CV and cover letter, with no anonymity step; the same form on 8 Dec 2004 asks authors to remove their name and affiliation (yalelawjournal.org: absent 25 Oct, present 7 Dec 2004); the bracket dates the request to authors, and the editor-in-chief of Vol. 117 (2008) called the process partial double-blind

journals.name: New York University Law Review
journals.basis: bracketed by archived pages: no anonymity statement in Mar 2021, Mar 2023 and Jan 2025; in Oct 2025 the page asks for anonymized manuscripts for email submissions, and the current page refers to an anonymous review process

journals.name: Arizona State Law Journal
journals.basis: bracketed by archived pages: the journal's submission page has full instructions and no anonymity statement in Feb and June 2025 (and in 2018-2024 copies); in Aug 2025 it asks authors to anonymize manuscripts, for the Fall 2025 cycle

journals.name: Stanford Law Review
journals.basis: earliest documented: Mar 2012 archived article instructions (Vol. 65) require names off the manuscript; explicit 'fully blind until the Committee's final vote' first seen Feb 2018 (Vol. 71); an Apr 2003 archived upload form has no anonymity step, so the instruction to authors began between 2003 and 2012

journals.name: Harvard Law Review
journals.basis: earliest documented (upper bound): the review's first website (gannett-netserv.law.harvard.edu, launched 1997) already states the policy in its earliest archived copy, Jan 1998; no earlier record, so no switch year; the review's 2025 fact sheet says names are hidden during the first two stages of review

journals.name: Tennessee Law Review
journals.basis: earliest documented (upper bound): the law school's Tennessee Law Review page says every submission is reviewed on an anonymous basis, without describing stages; the page was last modified in Mar 2024 (created 2015), so the statement was there by then at the latest

journals.name: Washington University Law Review
journals.basis: not dated: the current article pages (2026-10-31) ask for an anonymized manuscript together with an abstract and CV; the editor-in-chief (Sept 2026) calls the committee table read a blind review

journals.name: University of Chicago Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the submissions page says identifying information is removed before an article goes to outside peer review; it does not say the editors read anonymously and asks for no anonymized manuscript (not anonymous: inferred from the page)

journals.name: University of Pennsylvania Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): submit page asks for the author's CV with Articles and Essays and has no anonymity statement; Conklin (Nov 2021) reported the same

journals.name: Duke Law Journal
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the journal's Scholastica page asks for a cover letter with the author's name and affiliation; it mentions a 'double-blind peer review system' without saying the editors read anonymously

journals.name: Northwestern University Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): Scholastica author page requires a cover letter with the author's name and a CV or résumé; it has no anonymity statement for regular articles

journals.name: Vanderbilt Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): requires a cover letter and a CV or resume and has no anonymity statement; Thomson (c. 2019) reported the same

journals.name: California Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the Articles and Essays page asks for each author's name, mailing address, email, phone number and CV with the submission and has no anonymity statement

journals.name: Georgetown Law Journal
journals.basis: as of 2022: Conklin (2022 U. Ill. L. Rev. Online 1) quotes its article page asking for a CV and counts it among the 'top three non-blind' reviews; only student notes are selected anonymously

journals.name: Boston College Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): Submission Guidelines page asks for a resume or CV and a cover letter with the author's name and affiliation

journals.name: Notre Dame Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): submissions page requires a CV with every submission and says nothing about anonymity

journals.name: Boston University Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the review's Scholastica for-authors page asks for a cover letter and CV with each submission

journals.name: Southern California Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): submissions page asks for a CV with email-route submissions

journals.name: Ohio State Law Journal
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the submissions page on the law school site asks for a cover letter with the author's contact information and invites a CV, with no anonymity statement

journals.name: George Mason Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the review's current submission form asks for a CV for each author and has no anonymity statement

journals.name: Baylor Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the law-school page for the review asks for a cover letter with the author's name and affiliation and has no anonymity statement

journals.name: Alabama Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the review's Scholastica author page says the Acquisitions Committee weighs the author's past scholarship, which requires knowing who the author is (not anonymous: inferred from the page)

journals.name: Fordham Law Review
journals.basis: as of 2025: the review's submissions page (references the Volume 94 review starting Feb 2025) asks for a resume or CV with submissions and has no anonymity statement

journals.name: SMU Law Review
journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the submissions page lists a CV and a cover letter with author contact information among required items

journals.name: University of Illinois Law Review

journals.basis: current page (2026-10-31): the submission page asks for a CV for each author; Thomson (2019) listed it among reviews inviting or requiring a CV

journals.name: UC Davis Law Review

journals.name: UCLA Law Review
